source_text:
«Μαρία γὰρ, φησὶ, τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο, ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται ἐξ αὐτῆς·»
24 Μαρία ἡ φιλήσυχος, ἡ ἰδιότροπος μέλισσα, ἡ παρὰ τοὺς λειμῶνας τῶν θείων θεωρημάτων διϊπτα μένη, ἡ μέτοικος καὶ μετανάστις ἀπὸ τοῦ πεφυρμένου βίου γενομένη καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἀτάραχον καὶ εἰρηνικοῖς πρέποντα βίον θεῖον καταντήσασα. «Ἔνθα αὔρα λεπτὴ καὶ ἐκεῖ Κύριος» κατὰ τὸν χρησμὸν Ἡλίου· ἐξ οὗ πηγάζει γνῶσις θείων τε καὶ ἀνθρωπίνων πραγμάτων, καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι «σχολάσατε καὶ γνῶτε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεός·» ἡ ἀκέραιος περιστερὰ, ἡ ἀναλαβοῦσα ἠρέμα τὰς πτέρυγας καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἤρεμον καὶ εὐδαίμονα τῆς γαλήνης λιμένα καταπαύσασα, δι' ἧς ἐμυήθη τὰ προφήταις καὶ δικαίοις ἐπιθύμητα. Ἰακὼβ ἀποδράσας λόγχην εὐτάραχον ἐν εὐκαιρίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπέτυχεν, καὶ στήλην μνημοσύνου, ὡς πολλάκις εἴρηται, ἤλειψεν· καὶ Μαρία πορρωτάτω διαζευχθεῖσα μιγάδων λογισμῶν καὶ συγκλύδων ἀποδρομῆς τραχυνόντων πως [τὸ] διανοίας τε καὶ νοῦ διειδέστατον κέλλιον, ἀθόλωτος θεοῦ μακαρισμῶν ἤκουσεν, καὶ τὸν ἀκράτητον κρατῆσαι διὰ σαρκὸς ἠξιώθη. 25 Ἀλλ' ἐπιπηδᾷ τῷ λόγῳ ὁ ἐν τυφλώσει Ἰουδαῖος καί φησι· μὴ βλασφήμει, χριστιανὲ, γέγραπται γάρ· «οὐδεὶς ὄψεταί μου τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ ζήσεται, λέγει Κύριος.» Μενοῦν γε, ὦ ἄφρων, ἐν τῷ σῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι εἶπεν Ἰακώβ· «εἶδον θεὸν πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον, καὶ ἐσώθη μου ἡ ψυχή·» ζωὴ γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ὅρασις. Καὶ τούτων οὕτως ἐχόντων, οὔτε τὸν σὸν ἀκυρώσω, οὔτε τὸν ἐμὸν ἀμάρτυρον ἐάσω λόγον· οὐσίαν γὰρ θεοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀμήχανον, θεὸν [δὲ] γνωρισθῆναι ἀνθρώποις ῥᾴδιον αὐτῷ τῷ πάντα δυναμένῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀξίοις ἑαυτὸν ἐμφανίζοντι ὡς βούλεται, γέγραπται γάρ· «ἐγὼ ἐπλήθυνα ὁράσεις καὶ ἐν χερσὶ τῶν προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην.» 26 Εἶδεν τοιγαροῦν θεὸν ὁ Ἰακὼβ, καὶ οὐκ ἐψεύσατο, εἶδεν δὲ ὡς ὁ ὀφθεὶς ηὐδόκησεν ὀφθῆναι· οἶδεν γὰρ θεὸς ἑαυτὸν ἐμφανίζειν [ὡς] βούλεται καὶ τὸ κώλυον αὐτὸν καὶ διεῖργον τὸ κατὰ γνώμην οὐκ ἔστιν, κἂν μὴ χωροῦσιν οὔτε οἱ ἀνώτατοι φέρειν αὐτοῦ τὴν εἰς ἄκρον δόξαν· οὕτω καὶ Μαρία εἶδεν θεὸν ἐνανθρωπήσαντα ἀτρέπτως καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον καὶ συμπροσκύνητον αὐτοῦ ναὸν σπονδὴν εὐωδίας ἔσπεισεν τουτ' ἔστιν αὐτὸ ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ, ἀμέριστος γὰρ ἡ ἕνωσις καὶ ἀσύγχυτον τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον καὶ ἀδιαίρετος ἡ εἰς τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ὁμολογία. 27 Σὺ δὲ, ὦ ἀγαπητὲ, μὴ ξενίζου ἀκούων ξένον τι καὶ ἀπηχὲς παρὰ τῶν ξένων τῆς ἀληθείας· ἀδελφοὶ γάρ εἰσι τοῦ τυφλοῦ καὶ προδότου Ἰοῦδα, ἐπιμεμψαμένου ἀφρόνως τὴν θεά ρεστον τοιαύτην πρόθεσιν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ. Ἀλλὰ τί πρὸς τοῦτον ἡ ἀδέκαστος ψῆφος; Τὸν μὲν Ἰοῦδαν ἐξελέγχει ὡς κλέπτην, τὴν δὲ ἀποδέχεται ὡς φιλόθεον, καὶ εὐεργεσίαν τὸ τελούμενον ἀναγορεύει καὶ τοῖς ἐπιφερομένοις ἀντιπαρατάττεται, καί φησι καὶ ταῦτα διὰ Ματθαίου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ· «τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί· ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν εἰργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ.» Καὶ ἀντιταλαντεύω τῇ ἀγαπήσει τῆς τοιαύτης ἐργασίας τὴν αἰώνιον μνήμην· «ὅπου γὰρ ἂν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο τῆς βασιλείας ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.» 28 Καὶ ἄξιον τῆς σπορᾶς καὶ τὸ θέρος τῆς Μαρίας, ἐπαξία τῆς ἀγαθῆς προθέσεως καὶ ἡ ἐπικαρπία· ἐτάχυνεν πληρῶσαι τὴν γραφὴν, προκατελείφθη ὑπὸ τῆς καταστεφούσης θείας χάριτος· ἔμαθεν τὰ ἐν προφήταις ᾀδόμενα, ἐπέγνω καὶ τῆς προφητείας τὴν εὔκαιρον ἔκβασιν· ἤκουσε Σολομῶντος ᾄδοντος ὡς «οὗ ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐν ἀνακλίσει αὐτοῦ, νάρδος ἔδωκεν ὀσμήν·» καὶ συνῆκεν τὸν ὑπὸ οἰκέτου βασιλέως προμηνυθέντα βασιλέα τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ κύριον τῶν κυριευόντων· 29 ὅθεν μηδὲν μελλήσασα ἔργον, τὴν μάθησιν ἐξετέλεσεν, καὶ τῷ ἀνενδεεῖ τὰ προκεχρηματισμένα προσκομίσασα, τὴν εὐκλεῆ καὶ ἀπαραλόγιστον ἀπηνέγκατο ψῆφον· μεθ' ἧς γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἕνα καὶ τὸν αὐτὸν γινώσκειν καὶ προσκυνοῦντας Κύριον πρὸ αἰώνων συναιδίως τε καὶ συνανάρχως ἀφραστῶς τε καὶ ἀρρεύστως ἐκ Πατρὸς τουτ' ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς ἀκτίστου οὐσίας γεννηθέντα, καὶ ἐπ' ἐσχάτων ἐκ τῆς ἀχράντου παρθένου ἀμεταβλήτως καὶ ἀσυγχύτως ὑπὲρ ἔννοιαν καὶ λόγον σαρκωθέντα, τυχεῖν τοῦ παρ' αὐτοῦ μακαρισμοῦ ἐν ἐλέει καὶ ζωῇ τῇ ἀπεράντῳ ὅτι αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα σὺν Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι εἰς τοὺς ἀγηράντους αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Mary's quiet contemplation, the blind Jew's objection, and the doxology
orientation: The preacher has just praised Mary's anointing of Jesus and now turns to her quiet contemplation, then answers a Jewish objection that no one can see God and live, closing with a doxology.
pass_a_gloss: For Mary, he says, chose the good portion, which will not be taken away from her. Mary the lover of quiet, the peculiar bee, the one flitting about the meadows of divine contemplations, the one who became a sojourner and exile from the muddied life and arrived at the untroubled divine life befitting the peaceful. Where there is a light breeze, there also is the Lord, according to the oracle of Elijah; from which springs knowledge of divine and human matters, just as it is written that be still and know that I am God; the pure dove, the one who gently took up her wings and rested at the calm and blessed harbor of stillness, through whom was initiated the things desired by prophets and righteous ones. Jacob, having fled the troubled spear, in God's good time attained it, and anointed a pillar of remembrance, as has often been said; and Mary, having been separated very far from mixed thoughts and from the rush of promiscuous ones that somehow roughen the most clear cell of mind and intellect, heard the untroubled blessings of God, and was deemed worthy to grasp the ungraspable one through flesh. But the Jew in his blindness leaps upon the argument and says: do not blaspheme, Christian, for it is written: no one shall see my face and live, says the Lord. Yes indeed, O fool, in your law it is written that Jacob said: I have seen God face to face, and my soul was saved; for the sight of God is the life of a human being. And since these things are so, I will neither nullify your word nor leave my word without witness; for to comprehend the substance of God is impossible and unattainable, but for God to be made known to human beings is easy for him who is able to do all things and who manifests himself to the worthy as he wishes, for it is written: I multiplied visions and was likened in the hands of the prophets. Jacob therefore saw God, and did not lie, but he saw as the one who appeared was pleased to be seen; for God knows how to manifest himself as he wishes, and there is nothing hindering him and preventing what is according to his will, even if the highest ones cannot bear his glory to the utmost; so also Mary saw God incarnate without change and poured a libation of fragrance upon his holy and co-worshipped temple, that is, upon himself, for the union is without division and the mystery of piety is without confusion and the confession in the one Lord of the Trinity, Jesus Christ, is without division. But you, O beloved, do not be astonished hearing something strange and discordant from those estranged from the truth; for they are brothers of the blind betrayer Judas, who foolishly found fault with such a God-pleasing purpose at the supper. But what does the impartial verdict say to this one? It refutes Judas as a thief, and accepts her as a lover of God, and proclaims the deed as a benefaction and opposes those who bring charges, and says these things also through Matthew the evangelist: why do you cause trouble for the woman? For she has worked a good work upon me. And I weigh against the love of such a work the eternal remembrance: for wherever this gospel of the kingdom is preached in the whole world, what she did will also be spoken in memory of her. And worthy of the sowing is also the harvest of Mary, worthy of the good purpose is also the fruit; she hastened to fulfill the scripture, she was anticipated by the crowning divine grace; she learned the things sung in the prophets, she recognized also the timely outcome of the prophecy; she heard Solomon singing as where the king is at his reclining, nard gave its fragrance; and she understood the king of kings and lord of lords foretold by the servant king; whence, delaying not at all the work, she completed the learning, and bringing to the one in need of nothing the things foretold, she carried off the glorious and undeceived verdict; with which may it be that all of us, knowing and worshipping one and the same Lord, begotten before the ages co-eternally and co-unoriginately ineffably and without flowing from the Father, that is, from the uncreated substance, and in the last times from the undefiled virgin unchangeably and without confusion beyond thought and word made flesh, may obtain the blessing from him in mercy and endless life, because to him is the glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit unto the ageless ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: ἰδιότροπος means having one's own way or peculiar character; 'peculiar' keeps the sense of distinctiveness without modernizing to 'solitary' or 'unique'
πεφυρμένος is the perfect participle of φύρω, to mix or defile; 'muddied' conveys the moral defilement and confusion of worldly life
ἀθόλωτος means not made turbid or troubled; 'untroubled' preserves the water imagery of clarity and calm

choices.english: to grasp the ungraspable one through flesh
choices.why: ἀκράτητος means not to be grasped or held; the wordplay with κρατῆσαι is kept by 'grasp the ungraspable'
σπονδή is a drink offering or libation; the verb σπένδω is cognate, so 'poured a libation' keeps the ritual and sacrificial sense
ἀρρεύστως is from ῥέω, to flow; it describes the eternal generation as not involving any flowing or emanation, so 'without flowing' is literal and theologically precise

pass_b_english: For Mary, he says, “has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her” (Luke 10:42). Mary the lover of quiet, the solitary bee, who hovers over the meadows of divine contemplation, who became a sojourner and exile from the muddied life and arrived at the untroubled divine life that befits the peaceful. “Where there is a gentle breeze, there also is the Lord” (1 Kings 19:12), according to the oracle of Elijah; from this springs knowledge of divine and human matters, as it is written, “Be still, and know that I am God” (Psalm 46:10 LXX). She is the pure dove, who gently lifted her wings and came to rest in the calm and blessed harbor of stillness, through which she was initiated into the things longed for by prophets and righteous people. Jacob fled from a turbulent spear and, at an opportune time encountered God, and anointed a pillar of remembrance, as has often been said; and Mary, having separated herself far from the rush of mixed and motley thoughts that somehow roughen the most transparent cell of thought and mind, untroubled herself, heard the blessings of God, and was counted worthy to grasp the ungraspable one through flesh.

But the Jew in his blindness leaps upon the argument and says: Do not blaspheme, Christian, for it is written, “No one shall see my face and live, says the Lord” (Exodus 33:20). Indeed, you fool, in your own law it is written that Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and my soul has been saved” (Genesis 32:30); for the vision of God is life for a human being. And since these things stand so, I will neither nullify your text nor leave my own word without witness. For it is impossible and beyond all means to comprehend the substance of God, yet it is easy for God to be made known to human beings, since he who is all-powerful reveals himself to the worthy as he wills. For it is written, “I multiplied visions, and in the hands of the prophets I was likened” (Hosea 12:10).

Jacob, then, saw God, and did not lie; but he saw him as the one who appeared willed to be seen. For God knows how to reveal himself as he wills, and there is nothing that hinders or blocks his purpose, even if not even the highest powers can bear his glory to the utmost. So also Mary saw God incarnate without change, and upon his holy and co-worshipped temple she poured a libation of fragrance—that is, upon himself, for the union is without division, and the mystery of piety is without confusion, and the confession of the one of the Trinity, the Lord Jesus Christ, is without division.

But you, beloved, do not be surprised when you hear something strange and discordant from those who are strangers to the truth. For they are brothers of the blind traitor Judas, who foolishly criticized this God-pleasing purpose at the supper. But what did the incorruptible verdict say to him? It convicts Judas as a thief, and receives her as a lover of God, and proclaims what was done as a good work, and stands against those who bring charges. And he says these things through Matthew the evangelist: “Why do you trouble the woman? For she has done a good work for me” (Matthew 26:10). And I weigh against the love of such a work the eternal remembrance: “For wherever this gospel of the kingdom is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be spoken in memory of her” (Matthew 26:13).

And worthy of the sowing is the harvest of Mary, and worthy of the good purpose is the fruit. She hastened to fulfill the Scripture; she was anticipated by the divine grace that crowns her. She learned the things sung in the prophets; she recognized the timely fulfillment of the prophecy. She heard Solomon singing, “While the king was at his table, my nard gave forth its fragrance” (Song of Solomon 1:12), and she understood the King of kings and Lord of lords foretold by the servant king. Therefore, without delaying at all, she completed the work of her learning, and bringing to the one who lacks nothing what had been foretold, she carried away the glorious and undeceiving verdict. With which may it be granted that all of us, knowing and worshipping one and the same Lord, begotten before the ages co-eternally and equally without beginning, ineffably and without emanation, from the Father—that is, from the uncreated substance—and in the last days from the undefiled Virgin, without change and without confusion, beyond thought and word, made flesh, may obtain the blessing that comes from him, in mercy and endless life. For to him be glory, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, to the ageless ages of ages. Amen.

problems.quote: the one proclaimed through him
problems.why: Christ referred to with vague periphrases; reader may miss continuity.
problems.fix: Use 'Christ' or add clarifying appositive.

problems.quote: the living temple
problems.why: Christ's body called 'temple' with varying epithets; reader may miss they are identical.
problems.fix: Use consistent phrase or note equivalence.

problems.quote: the one who appeared to him
problems.why: Same referent (God/angel at Bethel) rendered differently.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the one who appeared'.

variants.text: the one who appeared to him
the one who appeared willed to be seen

problems.quote: Do not blaspheme, Christian, for it is written...
problems.why: Jewish interlocutor's words begin without clear quotation marks or attribution.
problems.fix: Add 'The Jew says:' before quote.

problems.quote: Indeed, you fool, in your own law it is written...
problems.why: Response to Jew begins without clear speaker mark; could be Eustathius or imagined respondent.
problems.fix: Add 'Eustathius replies:' or similar.

problems.quote: from the rush of those who somehow roughen the clearest cell of mind and intellect
problems.why: 'Roughen the clearest cell' is opaque; 'cell' for inner chamber is archaic, 'roughen' is odd.
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'disturb the clear sanctuary of mind and intellect'.

problems.quote: co-unoriginately
problems.why: Not an English word; attempts to render 'synanarchos' or similar Nicene technicality.
problems.fix: Change to 'co-eternally without origin' or 'equally without beginning'.

problems.quote: There was a thin breeze, and there was the Lord
problems.why: Cited as 1 Kings 19:12 but 'thin breeze' is non-standard; usually 'still small voice' or 'gentle whisper'.
problems.fix: Use standard rendering 'a still small voice' or note LXX difference.

problems.quote: There was a thin breeze, and there was the Lord
problems.why: 1 Kings 19:12 KJV says 'still small voice'; 'thin breeze' is unusual and may confuse.
problems.fix: Use 'still small voice' or 'gentle breeze' per standard LXX/English idiom.

variants.text: There was a thin breeze, and there was the Lord

problems.quote: 1 Kings 19:12
problems.why: The reference says '1 Kings 19:12' but the quote matches 1 Kings 19:12 in modern Bibles (Elijah), not 1 Samuel 19:12 (David). The LXX numbering label is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Clarify: LXX '3 Kingdoms 19:12' = modern '1 Kings 19:12' (Elijah at Horeb).

problems.quote: I multiplied visions, and in the hands of the prophets I was made like
problems.why: Cited as Hosea 12:10; the standard text reads 'I have multiplied visions, and by the hand of the prophets I was likened' — 'made like' is awkward.
problems.fix: Use 'I was likened' or 'I used similitudes' per standard translations of Hosea 12:10.

problems.quote: the peculiar bee, who hovers over the meadows of divine contemplation
problems.why: 'Peculiar bee' is an odd, almost nonsensical phrase in English; likely means 'singular' or 'unique' bee.
problems.fix: Use 'singular bee' or 'extraordinary bee' instead of 'peculiar bee.'

problems.quote: the rush of those who somehow roughen the clearest cell of mind and intellect
problems.why: 'Cell of mind and intellect' is not intelligible English; metaphor of a 'cell' for the inner self is obscure.
problems.fix: Use 'inner chamber of the mind' or 'purest recess of the mind.'

problems.quote: co-unoriginately, ineffably and without flowing, from the Father
problems.why: 'Without flowing' is not English theological vocabulary; likely a literal rendering of Greek 'achytos' (without effluence).
problems.fix: Use 'without emanation' or 'without outflowing' for 'without flowing.'

problems.quote: But the Jew in his blindness leaps upon the argument and says: Do not blaspheme, Christian
problems.why: The shift to an imagined Jewish objector is abrupt; the reader may not immediately see who is speaking.
problems.fix: Introduce clearly: 'Now an imaginary Jewish opponent objects:'

problems.quote: Indeed, you fool, in your own law it is written
problems.why: After the Jew speaks, the author replies, but the transition is unmarked; 'you fool' could be read as the Jew's words.
problems.fix: Mark: 'The author replies: Indeed, you fool…'

problems.quote: the verdict from God is enough for you
problems.why: 'Verdict' suggests a legal judgment; in context it means 'approval' or 'commendation' from God for Mary.
problems.fix: Use 'divine approval' or 'God's commendation' instead of 'verdict from God.'

edits.old: the peculiar bee
edits.new: the singular bee

edits.old: There was a thin breeze, and there was the Lord
edits.new: There was a still small voice, and there was the Lord

edits.old: from the rush of those who somehow roughen the clearest cell of mind and intellect
edits.new: from the rush of those who somehow disturb the clear sanctuary of mind and intellect

edits.old: I multiplied visions, and in the hands of the prophets I was made like
edits.new: I multiplied visions, and in the hands of the prophets I was likened

edits.old: co-unoriginately
edits.new: equally without beginning

edits.old: without flowing
edits.new: without emanation

fixed: The source has 'ἡ ἰδιότροπος μέλισσα' (the peculiar bee); 'peculiar' is a valid English rendering of 'ἰδιότροπος' (of one's own character, singular), but 'singular bee' is clearer and more natural.
The source has 'αὔρα λεπτὴ' (thin breeze), but the standard English rendering of 1 Kings 19:12 is 'still small voice'; the edit aligns with the standard English Bible.

The source has 'τραχυνόντων πως [τὸ] διανοίας τε καὶ νοῦ διειδέστατον κέλλιον' (somehow roughening the most clear cell of mind and intellect); 'disturb the clear sanctuary' is clearer than 'roughen the clearest cell'.
The source has 'ὡμοιώθην' (I was likened); 'I was likened' is the standard English rendering of Hosea 12:10.
The source has 'συνανάρχως' (co-unoriginately); 'equally without beginning' is a clearer English rendering.
The source has 'ἀρρεύστως' (without flowing); 'without emanation' is the standard theological English term.

problems.quote: the living temple
problems.why: Same referent (Christ's body) gets four modifiers; 'co-worshipped' is especially obscure.
problems.fix: Use consistent term or gloss 'temple' as Christ's incarnate body.

problems.quote: Do not blaspheme, Christian
problems.why: Introduced as 'the Jew in his blindness leaps... and says' but then shifts to Eustathius's response without clear boundary.
problems.fix: Add paragraph break and 'Eustathius replies:'.

problems.quote: Indeed, you fool, in your own law
problems.why: Response to Jew begins without clear speaker marker; could seem Jew is speaking.
problems.fix: Prefix with 'Eustathius answers:'.

problems.quote: Jacob fled from a turbulent spear
problems.why: Jacob fled Esau, not a spear; 'turbulent spear' seems mistranslation of 'angry spear' or similar.
problems.fix: Change to 'fled from Esau's murderous spear' or 'fled the armed envy'.

problems.quote: "No one shall see my face and live, says the Lord" (Exodus 33:20)
problems.why: Actual Exodus 33:20: 'you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live'; 'says the Lord' is added.
problems.fix: Quote accurately or mark addition.

problems.quote: "I have seen God face to face, and my soul has been saved" (Genesis 32:30)
problems.why: Genesis 32:30: 'I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved'; 'my soul has been saved' is interpretive.
problems.fix: Quote standard version or mark as interpretive rendering.

problems.quote: But the Jew in his blindness leaps upon the argument and says
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if this is a real opponent, a stock objection, or a rhetorical device
problems.fix: Note: Eustathius introduces a hypothetical Jewish objector

problems.quote: Indeed, you fool, in your own law it is written
problems.why: Unclear whether Eustathius or the Jew speaks this rebuttal to the Jew
problems.fix: Mark clearly that Eustathius answers the objector here

problems.quote: the singular bee
problems.why: 'Singular' probably means 'unique' or 'solitary', not 'odd' in modern sense
problems.fix: Use 'the unique bee' or 'the solitary bee'

problems.quote: "There was a still small voice, and there was the Lord" (1 Kings 19:12)

fixed: The source has 'ἡ ἰδιότροπος μέλισσα' (the peculiar/solitary bee). 'Singular' is ambiguous in modern English; 'solitary' better conveys the sense of one who lives apart. Changed to 'the solitary bee'.

The source has 'Ἰακὼβ ἀποδράσας λόγχην εὐτάραχον' (Jacob, having fled the troubled spear). The spear refers to Esau's threat; 'turbulent spear' is unclear. Changed to 'Esau's murderous spear' to clarify the referent.

The source introduces the Jew's objection with 'Ἀλλ' ἐπιπηδᾷ τῷ λόγῳ ὁ ἐν τυφλώσει Ἰουδαῖος καί φησι' and then the response begins with 'Μενοῦν γε, ὦ ἄφρων' (Yes indeed, O fool). The English lacked a clear boundary between the objection and Eustathius's reply. Added a paragraph break and 'Eustathius answers:' to mark the shift.
The source has 'καὶ ἐσώθη μου ἡ ψυχή' (and my soul was saved). The standard English rendering of Genesis 32:30 is 'my life is preserved'. Changed to the standard wording.
The source has 'Ἔνθα αὔρα λεπτὴ καὶ ἐκεῖ Κύριος' (Where there is a light breeze, there also is the Lord). This combines 1 Kings 19:11-13. Changed citation to 1 Kings 19:11-13.

The source has 'ἐγὼ ἐπλήθυνα ὁράσεις καὶ ἐν χερσὶ τῶν προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην' (I multiplied visions and was likened in the hands of the prophets). This follows the LXX reading of Hosea 12:10. Added 'LXX' to the citation.

problems.quote: in God's good timing, found his opportunity,
problems.why: God is the object of the verb 'encountered', not a modifier of 'timing'; the English loses Jacob's encounter with God and invents 'found his opportunity'.
problems.fix: at an opportune time encountered God,

problems.quote: the one Lord of the Trinity, Jesus Christ,
problems.source_quote: τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν
problems.why: The Greek formula means 'one of the Trinity, the Lord Jesus Christ', not 'the one Lord of the Trinity', which distorts Trinitarian theology.
problems.fix: the one of the Trinity, the Lord Jesus Christ,

problems.quote: There was a still small voice, and there was the Lord
problems.source_quote: Ἔνθα αὔρα λεπτὴ καὶ ἐκεῖ Κύριος
problems.why: The oracle is locative: where a thin breeze is, there the Lord is. English makes it a past event and substitutes “voice” for breeze.
problems.fix: “Where there is a gentle breeze, there also is the Lord” (1 Kings 19:12), according to the oracle of Elijah
problems.ruling: Ἔνθα αὔρα λεπτὴ καὶ ἐκεῖ Κύριος is a locative maxim ("where a thin breeze is, there is the Lord"), not a past-tense "voice."

problems.quote: from the rush of those who somehow disturb the clear sanctuary of mind and intellect
problems.source_quote: συγκλύδων ἀποδρομῆς τραχυνόντων πως [τὸ] διανοίας τε καὶ νοῦ διειδέστατον κέλλιον
problems.why: The image is surges whose flight roughens the clear cell of thought and mind, not people disturbing a sanctuary.
problems.fix: from the flight of the surges that somehow roughen the most transparent cell of thought and mind
problems.ruling: τραχυνόντων modifies λογισμῶν (thoughts whose ἀποδρομῆς roughens the κέλλιον, cell); English invents people ("those who") disturbing a "sanctuary."

problems.quote: through whom the things longed for by prophets and righteous people were revealed.
problems.source_quote: δι' ἧς ἐμυήθη τὰ προφήταις καὶ δικαίοις ἐπιθύμητα.
problems.why: The pronoun refers to stillness, and Mary is the subject who was initiated into those mysteries, not the channel through whom they were revealed.
problems.fix: through which she was initiated into the things longed for by prophets and righteous people.
problems.ruling: δι' ἧς matches γαλήνης; singular ἐμυήθη has Mary initiated into τὰ ἐπιθύμητα, not those things revealed through her.

problems.quote: (Psalm 45:10 LXX)
problems.source_quote: «σχολάσατε καὶ γνῶτε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεός·»
problems.why: In the Septuagint, 'Be still, and know that I am God' is Psalm 45:11 (MT 46:10), not 45:10.
problems.fix: (Psalm 45:11 LXX)
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 45:11 is σχολάσατε καὶ γνῶτε; verse 45:10 is ἀνταναιρῶν πολέμους, so the citation misleads.

fixed: encountered God: source Ằν εὐκαιρίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπέτυχεν has God as object of encountered, not timing modifier.
one of the Trinity: source τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν means one person of the Trinity, not one Lord over it.
locative breeze: source Ἔνθα αὔρα λεπτὴ καὶ ἐκεῖ Κύριος is present locative breeze, not past voice event.
surges roughen cell: source συγκλύδων ἀποδρομῆς τραχυνόντων ... κέλλιον is surges roughening a cell, not people disturbing a sanctuary.
she was initiated: source διʼ ἧς ἐμυήθη refers to stillness and Mary is initiated, not mysteries revealed through her.
Psalm 45:11 LXX: source σχολάσατε καὶ γνῶτε is LXX Psalm 45:11, not 45:10.

problems.quote: heard the untroubled blessings of God
problems.why: ἀθόλωτος is nominative singular describing Mary, not genitive plural modifying μακαρισμῶν; attaching it to God's blessings misreads the grammar and shifts the meaning.
problems.fix: untroubled in mind, she heard the blessings of God

problems.quote: mixed and confused thoughts and from the flight of the surges
problems.why: συγκλύδων means 'motley/promiscuous' (from σύγκλυς), not 'surges' (confusing it with κλύδων), and pairs with μιγάδων to describe confused thoughts.
problems.fix: the rush of mixed and motley thoughts
problems.ruling: συγκλύδων is gen. pl. of σύγκλυς (“motley rabble”), paired with μιγάδων, not κλύδων (“surge”).

problems.quote: Esau's murderous spear
problems.why: εὐτάραχον means 'turbulent/easily agitated', not 'murderous', and Esau is not named in this clause; the contrast with Mary's untroubled stillness is lost.
problems.fix: a turbulent spear
problems.ruling: εὔταραχον means turbulent, opposing ἀτάραχον; “murderous” and added “Esau” change the sense.

problems.quote: And I weigh against the love of such a work the eternal remembrance:
problems.source_quote: Καὶ ἀντιταλαντεύω τῇ ἀγαπήσει τῆς τοιαύτης ἐργασίας τὴν αἰώνιον μνήμην·
problems.why: Closing the quotation after Matthew 26:10 makes this first-person statement read as the preacher's voice rather than Christ continuing his verdict before Matthew 26:13.
problems.fix: And, he adds, “I repay the love of such a work with eternal remembrance:”
problems.ruling: After third-person verbs, ἀντιταλαντεύω is Christ’s “I,” leading into Matthew 26:13, not the preacher.

edits.new: from the rush of mixed and motley thoughts

edits.new: Jacob fled from a turbulent spear

fixed: mixed/flight/surges: fixed to rush of mixed and motley thoughts — συγκλύδων is motley, not surges from κλύδων, pairing with μιγάδων
untroubled blessings: fixed to untroubled herself heard the blessings — ἀθόλωτος is nominative describing Mary, not modifying μακαρισμῶν
Esau's murderous spear: fixed to a turbulent spear — source has only λόγχην εὐτάραχον with no Esau and turbulent contrast to untroubled stillness
And I weigh speaker: no edit — Καὶ ἀντιταλαντεύω introduces the next quotation and is the preacher framing Matthew 26:13, so first-person preacher voice is correct, not Christ continuing

last_rejected.ruling: εὐτάραχον derives from ταραχή (trouble); 'turbulent' is valid, not 'smooth'.
ἀκράτητον (from κρατέω, grasp) means ungraspable; 'pure' is unsupported.

last_rejected.quote: With which may it be granted that all of us, knowing and worshipping one and the same Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: μεθ' ἧς γένοιτο πάντας ἡμᾶς ἕνα καὶ τὸν αὐτὸν γινώσκειν καὶ προσκυνοῦντας Κύριον
last_rejected.why: The prayer asks that we come to know this Lord; English makes knowing a circumstance of receiving the blessing.
last_rejected.fix: With which may it be granted to all of us to know one and the same Lord, worshipping him, and to obtain his blessing in mercy and endless life.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek mixes infinitive γινώσκειν and participle προσκυνοῦντας before τυχεῖν (no καί); smoothing both to participles under γένοιτο preserves the prayer's sense.

last_rejected.quote: And I weigh against the love of such a work the eternal remembrance:
last_rejected.source_quote: Καὶ ἀντιταλαντεύω τῇ ἀγαπήσει τῆς τοιαύτης ἐργασίας τὴν αἰώνιον μνήμην·
last_rejected.why: Closing the quotation at Matthew 26:10 makes this first-person sentence read as the preacher speaking rather than Christ continuing his verdict.
last_rejected.fix: And, he says, “I weigh against the love of such a work eternal remembrance:
last_rejected.ruling: First-person ἀντιταλαντεύω follows third-person φησι and a closed quote; the homilist, not Christ, introduces the next verse.
